messages:
dana: Quick follow-up from the tenant-multiplexor RFC — want to lock down a migration runway this quarter. The problem: the multiplexor currently owns routing, billing tags, telemetry enrichment, and a tiny feature-flag layer. It's accreted responsibilities and is blocking a few infra optimizations.
ryan: +1. Can you restate the concrete success criteria? latency, deploy safety, and ownership split?
dana: Exactly. Success criteria: 1) no regression in p50/p95 latency for hot tenants, 2) zero billing tag loss during cutover, 3) clear ownership for routing vs billing (two teams), 4) rollout can be reverted quickly. Also need a plan for live traffic validation.
sophia: Three high-level options we discussed in the RFC — putting them here so people can pick: A) Per-tenant sidecars (isolate state, easiest ownership but infra cost), B) Thin router + plugin hooks (single runtime, plugin isolation, faster rollout), C) Facade->extract (gradual pull-out of billing/enrichment into a separate service w/compat shim). I'm leaning B for speed, C for long-term clarity.
kevin: Concern with B: the plugin surface touches KV access patterns. If we keep single runtime, contention might spike under large bursts. Do we have load numbers to simulate? :thinking_face:
dana: We ran two replayed traces on staging yesterday. Quick numbers: with 10k rps mix (50% hot tenants) the single runtime plugin variant showed +8% p95 under worst-case bursts vs baseline. Sidecars kept p95 flat but increased infra cpu by ~1.6x. Raw logs attached in staging run 2026-03-19. arch-bot: replay-summary uploaded -> https://ci.internal/replays/1714989999
mira: For billing tags: whatever we do we must guarantee at-least-once enrichment to the event stream (we can't drop tags). That means either sync writes to event-lag buffer or durable prewrite. Suggest strategy: write tags to small per-tenant append log before acking request. That can be a short-lived contract during migration.
sophia: That prewrite adds latency. Could we do a conditional async path: if tenant is in canary set then prewrite sync, otherwise async best-effort, then fast-failover to prewrite if we detect tag loss? We can flip a feature flag per tenant-group.
dryan: @dana can we clarify rollback plan? If we extract billing into service, how do we fail back to multiplexor quickly if enrichment pipeline lags?
dana: Rollback approach: keep multiplexor enrichment as an active fallback path for 4 weeks after cutover. Traffic routing will use weighted split (canary) controlled in the control plane. If newly extracted path falls behind (defined by tag delivery lag metric > 5s for 5m window) the control plane instantly routes that tenant back through the fallback. No CPU or memory migration required for fallback because multiplexor will be still running parallel but no-op for normal tenants.
kevin: Need a concrete canary schedule. Suggest: week 0: internal-only tenants, week 1: 1% production tenants (low qps), week 2: 10%, week 3: 50%, week 4: ramp to 100% and keep fallback for 4 more weeks.
mira: Agree. Also add a verification step after each ramp: verify billing totals match within 0.1% and that SLOs hold. Add smoke prompt set and diff tool.
sophia: Example shim pseudo-config for thin-router plugin (so infra knows exact surface):
```yaml
router:
  plugins:
    - name: billing-enrich
      api:
        enrich(request): -> { tags }
      failure_mode: failopen  # or failclosed during canary
```
dana: FYI: failure_mode will be toggled per-phase. During canary we run `failclosed` for canary tenants to get strong guarantees; after 50% we can relax to `failopen` and rely on fallback detection.
ryan: Testing strategy: 1) unit tests for plugin contract, 2) integration harness that replays historical 72h traffic with the plugin enabled, 3) chaos test: drop enrichment service for 30s and verify fallback engages. Who owns tests?
dana: Ownership: infra-team owns routing surface & plugin harness, billing-team owns extraction service + tag contract. We'll create a cross-team playbook and a weekly sync. I'll spin up a JIRA epic and assign owners.
kevin: One last ops ask: instrumentation. For each tenant we need per-minute counters: enrich_success, enrich_latency_ms_p50/p95, fallback_trigger_count. Also add a histogram for downstream event lag. We need these exposed to dashboards and alerting.
mira: Agreed. I'll add dashboards and an alert: if enrich_latency_p95 > 500ms for 5m or fallback_trigger_count > 0 for prod tenants -> page oncall.
sophia: Small implementation note — secret access: the enrichment service needs read-only access to tenant-metadata. Use short-lived tokens minted by control plane; do not grant broad RBAC.
arch-bot: CI checks: migration-epic created -> REDWOOD-1234, replay-test job queued -> https://ci.internal/jobs/1715002234
dana: Next steps: 1) finalize migration playbook w/ dates in REDWOOD-1234, 2) infra to implement plugin surface (sophia + kevin), 3) billing to prototype extraction service and prewrite strategy (mira), 4) run replay tests (ryan). Can we aim to start week-of 2026-04-06 for internal canary?
ryan: Week-of 04/06 works for infra timeline. :thumbsup:
mira: billing ok to prep but need one extra engineer for 2 weeks in April. I'll file headcount request.
sophia: I'll draft the plugin PR and link to REDWOOD-1234 by EOD Friday.
dana: Great. I'll drop the playbook doc in the migration folder and ping everyone. Thanks! :rocket:
